mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted, {يَا أَيهَا النَّاس}: أيّ is a singular vocative (nidāʾ mufrad), and هَا is for drawing attention (tanbīh). According to Sībawayh nothing but the nominative is permitted in النَّاس, and it is a naʿt (adjective) of the singular [vocative], because it is indispensable and it is the one addressed in meaning. Al-Māzinī permitted the accusative in it according to the position of أيّ, because the one addressed is a direct object in meaning. It [أيّ] has ḍamma only because it is indeclinable (mabnī), and it was made indeclinable only because it occurs in the position of the one spoken to, and the one spoken to is never an overt noun, only a pronoun, a kāf or a tāʾ. The proof that the one addressed is spoken to is that if you said "By Allah, I will not speak to Zayd" and then said "O Zayd!", you would break your oath, because it is speaking to him. So since it occurs in the position of the pronoun, it was made indeclinable, just as the pronoun is always indeclinable. But in its origin it is fully declinable, so it was made indeclinable on a vowel, and ḍamma was chosen for it because of its strength; and it is said: because of its resemblance to قبل and بعد. There are other views on the reason for its ḍamma besides these, whose mention would be lengthy.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {وَأَن الله}: أَن is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to بِمَا. It is also said that أَن is in the position of the nominative in the meaning "and the matter is that Allah…" (وَالْأَمر أَن الله). The kasra [إنّ] as a new beginning (istiʾnāf) is good.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying {يَدْعُو لمن ضره أقرب من نَفعه}: al-Kisāʾī said: the lām is out of its place, and مَن is in the position of the accusative by يدعو; the implied form is "he calls upon one whose harm is surely nearer than his benefit" (يَدْعُو من لضره أقرب من نَفعه), i.e. he calls upon a god whose harm is surely nearer than its benefit. Al-Mubarrad said: there is an omitted object in the speech, and the lām is in its place; مَن is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), ضره is a mubtadaʾ, أقرب its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of مَن, and {لبئس الْمولى} is the khabar of مَن; its implied form is "he calls upon a god; surely the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit — what an evil patron!" (يَدْعُو إِلَهًا لمن ضره أقرب من نَفعه لبئس الْمولى). Al-Akhfash said: يدعو has the meaning of يقول ("says"), and مَن is a mubtadaʾ, ضره a second mubtadaʾ, أقرب its khabar, and the clause is the ṣila of مَن, and the khabar of مَن is omitted, its implied form being "he says: the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit is his god" (يَقُول لمن ضره أقرب من نَفعه إلهه). We have explained this question in a separate book, because there is room for consideration in it and objections to these views, and there are other views on it besides these. It is a difficult (mushkil) question on which much can be said, and for that reason disagreement about it is abundant.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {إِن الَّذين آمنُوا وَالَّذين هادوا}: the khabar (predicate) of إن is His saying {إِن الله يفصل}. The Basrans permitted إن زيدا إنه منطلق ("Zayd — he is departing"), just as إن زيدا هو منطلق is permitted. Al-Farrāʾ prohibited it, but permitted it in the verse because it contains the meaning of requital (jazāʾ), so he took the khabar according to the meaning.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {وَكثير حق عَلَيْهِ الْعَذَاب}: كثير is nominative, conjoined to مَن in His saying {يسْجد لَهُ من}. That is permissible because prostration is humbling oneself and submitting; so the unbelievers upon whom the punishment has become due are humbled under the decree of Allah and His disposal, and they submit to what was foreordained concerning them in Allah's knowledge, not departing from what was foreordained concerning them in Allah's knowledge. It is also said that كثير is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is the khabar (predicate). The accusative is permissible, as He said {والظالمين أعد لَهُم عذَابا أَلِيمًا}, by an implied verb, as though He said "and He humiliated many upon whom the punishment became due" or "and He created many upon whom the punishment became due", and the like of such implied forms which the meaning indicates. The nominative was preferred in it according to al-Kisāʾī only because it is taken according to the meaning of the verb, since its meaning is "and many refused to prostrate".

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {يصهر بِهِ مَا فِي بطونهم}: مَا is in the position of the nominative by يصهر (as nāʾib fāʿil), and {والجلود} is conjoined to {مَا}; the meaning is "by it what is in their bellies is melted, and by it their skins are melted". The hāʾ in {بِهِ} refers back to {الْحَمِيم}.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His saying {إِن الَّذين كفرُوا ويصدون}: {ويصدون}, which is imperfect, was conjoined to {كفرُوا}, which is past, only because يصدون is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the past may be a ḥāl together with قد. It is also said that it is conjoined according to the meaning, because its implied form is "those who disbelieve and those who bar" (إن الْكَافرين والصادين). It is said that the wāw is redundant (zāʾida) and يصدون is the khabar of إن. And it is said that the khabar of إن is omitted, its implied form being "those who disbelieved and did such and such have lost and perished", and the like of such implied forms which the speech indicates.
His saying {سَوَاء العاكف فِيهِ والباد}: سَوَاء is nominative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the resident in it and the visitor are equal" (العاكف والبادي فِيهِ سَوَاء). In this reading there is evidence that the Sanctuary (al-Ḥaram) is not owned, because Allah the Exalted has made the resident and others equal in it. It is also said that {سَوَاء} is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and {العاكف} is nominative by its verbal sense and stands in place of the khabar; and there is remoteness in this, because you would have to make سواء have the meaning of مستو ("equal"), and for that reason it governs; but it is not good for مستو to govern until it leans on something before it. If you make سواء and what follows it in the position of the second object of جعلنا, it becomes good for it to be nominative as a mubtadaʾ and to have the meaning of مستو [Translator's note: the source writes يمعنى for بمعنى], so that you make العاكف nominative by it and it stands in place of the khabar.
Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read it in the accusative, making it a maṣdar (verbal noun) governed by the meaning of جعلنا, as though He said "We made it equal for the people, an equality" (سويناه للنَّاس سَوَاء), and العاكف is made nominative by it, i.e. with the resident being equal in it. The maṣdar comes with the meaning of the active participle; so سواء, even though it is a maṣdar, has the meaning of مستو, as one says رجل عدل meaning عادل ("just"). On that basis Sībawayh and others permitted مَرَرْت بِرَجُل سَوَاء درهمه ("I passed by a man whose dirham is all the same") and بِرَجُل سَوَاء هُوَ والعدم ("by a man who and nothingness are equal"), i.e. مستو. It is also permissible to make سواء accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun assumed together with the preposition in
His saying {للنَّاس}, with the adverbial phrase (ẓarf) governing it; or from the hāʾ in {جَعَلْنَاهُ}, with جعلنا governing it. It is also permissible to make it accusative as the second object of جعلنا, and to put {العاكف} in the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of النَّاس or as a badal (substitute). It has been read with العاكف in the genitive as a badal from النَّاس; and it is said: as a naʿt, because النَّاس is a genus among the genera of creatures: "We made it equal for the one resident in it and the visitor".
His saying {وَمن يرد فِيهِ بإلحاد بظُلْم}: the bāʾ in {بإلحاد} is redundant (zāʾida), and the bāʾ in {بظُلْم} is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يرد.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying {كتب عَلَيْهِ أَنه من تولاه}: أَن is in the position of the nominative by كتب (as nāʾib fāʿil).
And His saying {فَأَنَّهُ يضله}: al-Zajjāj mentioned that the second أن is conjoined to the first, in the position of the nominative. Then he said: as for the fāʾ, the best is that it be in the position of the requital (jazāʾ). Then he went back and undid that, and said: the reality of the second أن is that it is repeated by way of emphasis (tawkīd), because the meaning is "it was written concerning Satan that whoever takes him as a patron, he will lead him astray".
He was criticised for permitting the fāʾ to be conjunctive, because {من تولاه} is a condition and the fāʾ is the answer of the condition, and conjoining to the first أن is not permissible until it is complete, because what follows it belongs to its ṣila; so if it is not complete with its ṣila, conjoining to it is not permissible, since nothing is conjoined to a relative (mawṣūl) until it is complete; and the condition and its answer in this verse are together the khabar of the first أن. He was also criticised for his saying that the second أن is repeated for emphasis; and it was said: how can it be for emphasis when the thing emphasised is not complete? Emphasis is only proper after the thing emphasised is complete, and the first أن is complete at His saying {السعير}.
The correct view on the second أن is that it is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it was written concerning Satan that whoever takes him as a patron, then his affair is that he leads him astray" (فَشَأْنه أَنه يضله), or "then his matter is that he leads him astray", i.e. his affair is leading astray. It is also possible that the second أن is in the position of the nominative by the [implied] being-settled (al-istiqrār), if you imply له, its implied form being "it was written concerning him that whoever takes him as a patron, then for him is that he leads him astray" (فَلهُ أَنه يضله), i.e. for him is his leading him astray and guiding him to the punishment of the Blaze.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying {ذَلِك بِأَن الله هُوَ الْحق}: ذا is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the matter is that" (الْأَمر ذَلِك). Al-Zajjāj permitted ذا to be in the position of the accusative, in the meaning "Allah did that because He is the Truth" (فعل الله ذَلِك بِأَنَّهُ الْحق).

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying {ثَانِي عطفه}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يُجَادِل, which refers back to مَن in His saying من يُجَادِل; its meaning is "he disputes about the signs of Allah without knowledge, turning away from the reminder". His saying {ذَلِك بِمَا قدمت}: ذَلِك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and بما قدمت the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:26-26.t:
His saying {وَإِذ بوأنا لإِبْرَاهِيم}: the lām entered upon إبراهيم only on the basis that بوأت is taken in the meaning of جعلت ("We made/appointed"), for the basic usage of بوأ is that it does not take its object through a preposition. It is also said that the lām is redundant (zāʾida); and it is said that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).
His saying {أَن لَا تشرك}: i.e. بأن لا ("that you should not…"), so it is in the position of the accusative. It is also said that it is redundant for emphasis; and it is said that it has the meaning of أي, for explanation (tafsīr).

mekki-muskil:27-27.t: His saying {وعَلى كل ضامر يَأْتِين}: يأتين (plural) was said only because ضامر has the meaning of a plural and كل indicates generality, so the predicate came according to the meaning, in the plural form. Ibn Masʿūd read يأتون, referring it back to النَّاس.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {من الْأَوْثَان}: مِن is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins). Al-Akhfash made it partitive (tabʿīḍ), in the meaning "so avoid the filth which is part of the idols". For whoever makes مِن clarify the genus, its meaning is "so avoid the filth of which the idols are [a kind]", and this is more general in the prohibition and more fitting.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t:
His saying {حنفَاء لله}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in {اجتنبوا}, and likewise {غير مُشْرِكين}.
His saying {فتخطفه الطير}: whoever reads it with the ṭāʾ doubled, its origin for him is فتتخطفه on the pattern تتفعل; then one of the two tāʾs was dropped for lightness because their vowels agree. Whoever reads it light builds it on خطف يخطف, as Allah the Exalted said {إِلَّا من خطف الْخَطفَة}. There are irregular (shādhdh) and well-known readings in it whose explanation would be lengthy.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying {ذَلِك وَمن يعظم}: ذا is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its meaning being "the matter is that" (الْأَمر ذَلِك); or as a mubtadaʾ in the meaning "that is the matter" (ذَلِك الْأَمر). It is also said that the position of ذا is accusative, in the meaning "follow that of Allah's command" (اتبعُوا ذَلِك من أَمر الله).

mekki-muskil:36-36.t:
His saying {وَالْبدن}: the plural of بَدَن, like وَثَن and وُثْن; the single one is called بَدَن. It is also said that it is the plural of بَدَنة, like خَشَبة and خُشُب, and on this view the second letter may take ḍamma, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it so. Quiescence is better, because it is originally an adjective, since it is derived from البدانة (corpulence), and it is not like خشبة and خشب, because this is a noun, so ḍamma in it is better.
His saying {صواف}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), but it is a diptote because it is on the pattern فواعل, so it is a plural which has no counterpart in the singular; it is barred from full declension for these two reasons. Its meaning is "lined up". Al-Ḥasan and others read it صوافيَ with a yāʾ bearing fatḥa, accusative as a ḥāl, and its meaning is "purely for Allah, free of associating partners", so it is derived from الصفاء (purity). Qatāda read it صَوَافِن with nūn; the meaning of الصافنة is the one that has drawn its legs together and raised the tips of its hooves; and it is said that it is the one hobbled with ropes for slaughter. الصافن is a vein at the front of the horse's leg; when it is struck upon, it raises its leg.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t: And His saying {إِلَّا أَن يَقُولُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative because it has the meaning of "except because they say" (إلا بِأَن يَقُولُوا).

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {الَّذين إِن مكناهم}: الَّذين is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from مَن in His saying {ولينصرن الله من ينصره}; and they are Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them.

mekki-muskil:45-45.t: His saying {وبئر معطلة}: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to قرية; and it is said to be conjoined to العروش.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t:
His saying {ألم تَرَ أَن الله أنزل من السَّمَاء مَاء فَتُصْبِح الأَرْض مخضرة}: according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl this speech is a statement (khabar), and the fāʾ is not an answer to His saying {ألم تَرَ}; the meaning according to them is "Take heed, O son of Ādam: Allah sent down water from the sky, and from it such and such came about"; for that reason {فَتُصْبِح} came in the nominative. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is a statement, and its meaning is "Know that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green".
His saying {مِلَّة أبيكم}: ملة is accusative by implying "follow the creed of your father" (اتبعُوا مِلَّة أبيكم). Al-Farrāʾ said: it is accusative by the omission of the preposition, its implied form being "like the creed of your father" (كملة أبيكم); when the preposition was omitted it became accusative. Its implied form according to him is "He has made the religion spacious for you, like the creed of your father", because {وَمَا جعل عَلَيْكُم فِي الدّين من حرج} indicates "He has made it spacious for you". This is a remote view.

mekki-muskil:65-65.t: His saying {أَن تقع على الأَرْض}: أَن is in the position of the accusative in the meaning "out of aversion to its falling", "so that it does not fall", and "for fear of its falling".

mekki-muskil:78-78.t:
His saying {هُوَ سَمَّاكُم الْمُسلمين}: هُوَ refers to Allah (exalted be His mention) according to most of the exegetes; and al-Ḥasan said: it refers to Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him).
And His saying {وَفِي هَذَا}: i.e. "and He named you Muslims in this Qurʾān"; and the pronoun in سماكم likewise admits both views.
